writing.title: Notice Writing
writing.html:
📌 What is a Notice?

A notice is a formal, concise piece of writing used by institutions, schools, or organizations to announce events, issue instructions, or make appeals to a targeted audience. It must be brief, factual, and to the point.

📝 Format / Structure (Word Limit: 50 words)

A notice MUST be enclosed in a BOX. 

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                        NAME OF THE INSTITUTION/SCHOOL                       |
|                                                                             |
|                                  NOTICE                                     |
|                                                                             |
| Date (e.g., 14 May 2026)                                                    |
|                                                                             |
|                             HEADING / TITLE                                 |
|                                                                             |
| Body of the Notice: (Target audience, what the event is, date, time, venue, |
| and whom to contact for further details. Keep it brief and to the point.)   |
|                                                                             |
| Signature                                                                   |
| Name                                                                        |
| Designation                                                                 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

⚖️ CBSE Marking Scheme (Typically 3 Marks)

  • Format: 1 Mark (Box, Name of Institution, "NOTICE", Date, Heading, Name/Designation)
  • Content: 1 Marks (What, When, Where, Whom to contact)
  • Expression: 1 Mark (Grammar, Spelling, Formal Tone)

💡 Language Tips & Key Rules

  • Tone: Formal and objective. Avoid first-person pronouns (I, we) unless used in the designation (e.g., "The undersigned").
  • Passive Voice: Prefer passive structures (e.g., It is hereby notified that... or Students are informed that...).
  • The 5 Ws: Ensure your notice answers: What is the event? Where is the venue? When is the date and time? Who is eligible? Whom to contact?
  • Word Limit: Strictly adhere to the 50-word limit for the body.

⚠️ Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Forgetting the Box: This is a guaranteed deduction of marks.
  • Informal language: Do not use conversational greetings like "Hello friends".
  • Missing deadlines: If an event requires registration, always mention a "last date to register".

🌟 Model Example

Q: You are the Cultural Secretary of Bal Bharati Public School, Delhi. Your school is organizing an Inter-House Dramatics Competition. Write a notice in about 50 words inviting names from students of Classes IX and X. 

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                        BAL BHARATI PUBLIC SCHOOL, DELHI                     |
|                                                                             |
|                                    NOTICE                                   |
|                                                                             |
| 20 August 2026                                                              |
|                                                                             |
|                       INTER-HOUSE DRAMATICS COMPETITION                     |
|                                                                             |
| This is to inform all students of Classes IX and X that the school is       |
| organizing an Inter-House Dramatics Competition on 5 September 2026 in the  |
| school auditorium from 10:00 AM onwards. The theme for the play is "Unity   |
| in Diversity". Interested students must register their names with their     |
| respective House Captains latest by 28 August 2026.                         |
|                                                                             |
| (Signature)                                                                 |
| Kavita Sharma                                                               |
| Cultural Secretary                                                          |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

✍️ Practice Prompts

  1. Tour/Camp: You are the Sports Captain. Write a notice informing students of Class IX about a 3-day Trekking Camp to Shimla. Mention dates, fees, and the last date for submitting consent forms.
  2. Found: You found a silver wristwatch in the school computer lab. Write a notice for the school notice board asking the rightful owner to claim it by providing necessary identification details.

writing.title: Narrative Writing
writing.html:
A short story is a powerful form of fiction that can leave a strong impression on the reader even though the writer works with a limited number of words. There are no set guidelines to being a successful writer, but it helps to keep a few points in mind when writing a short story.

  • Purpose
    • to entertain and enthral
  • Structure
    • a lively opening that will engage the reader
    • clear story structure—main characters and setting
    • a complication/turning points
    • resulting events
    • resolution of the complication
    • ending has to be linked with the opening
  • Language features
    • written in first person or third person
    • written in past tense
    • ideas organised into proper, clear sentences
    • a variety of sentence structures (direct speech, passive voice, simple, compound and complex sentences, etc.) to maintain the reader's interest
    • largely chronological but may contain flashbacks
    • distinctive characters

Now, attempt writing short stories along these guidelines.
1. Write an original short story to bring out the meaning of the proverb—Blood is thicker than water.
2. Write an original short story which has as its theme—Women can be every bit as brave as men.
3. Write an original short story beginning with, 'I never expected this from you...'
4. Write an original short story where a beggar, a dog and a baby play important roles.
5. Write an original short story entitled, 'Winds of Change'.
6. Write an original short story concluding with the following line— 'I just didn't know what to say!'
7. 'As the sun rose on the changed landscape...'—complete the short story.
8. Write an original short story entitled, 'The Forbidden Cupboard'.
9. Write an original short story ending with the line—'And then I woke up.'
10. Write an original short story where a clown, a doctor and an asylum play important roles.

Answers – Narrative Writing

Exercise

  1. Blood Is Thicker Than Water

Arjun and Karan were brothers separated by years of bitter business rivalry. Though raised in the same modest house, their differing ambitions led to a painful rift. They built competing textile firms in the city and had not spoken a word to each other in five years.

One stormy night, a massive electrical short-circuit triggered a raging fire in Karan's warehouse. As alarm bells chimed across the industrial park, workers scrambled out, but Karan remained trapped on the upper floor while trying to retrieve critical financial ledgers.

News of the blaze reached Arjun at his home. Ignoring his manager's advice to stay clear, Arjun sprinted into the rain and drove frantically to the site. Overcoming thick smoke and falling timber, Arjun wrapped a wet coat around himself, forced open the emergency door, and dragged his unconscious brother out to safety just moments before the roof collapsed. When Karan opened his eyes in the ambulance and saw his brother weeping beside him, all former grudges evaporated into tears of reconciliation. Family bonds, they realized, ran deeper than any worldly dispute.

  1. Bravery Knows No Gender

The snowstorm over the Kumaon hills had grounded all civilian aircraft. A group of four trekkers were stranded at twelve thousand feet, suffering from severe frostbite, and time was running out. Two senior male pilots had deemed an airlift mission impossible due to violent tailwinds.

Flight Lieutenant Sunita Sharma stepped forward without hesitation. 'I know the valley terrain like the back of my hand, Chief. Give me ten minutes,' she urged her commanding officer. Despite skepticism from her peers, she maneuvered her rescue chopper through dense fog and turbulent air currents with extraordinary precision.

Reaching the narrow ridge, she held the helicopter in a steady hover inches above the snowbanks. Within twenty minutes, all four trekkers were hoisted safely into the cabin. As the chopper touched down safely at the base hospital, the chief officer saluted Sunita respectfully. She had proved beyond a shadow of a doubt that courage and skill know no gender boundaries.

  1. An Unexpected Sacrifice

'I never expected this from you...' Rohan whispered, staring at his best friend Sameer in disbelief.

The computer laboratory room was quiet, save for the hum of the cooling fan. Ten minutes earlier, a rare electronic testing kit worth thousands of rupees had slipped from Rohan's nervous hands, shattering on the tiled floor. Panic had seized Rohan, for a prior warning meant he faced immediate expulsion from school.

Just as the principal entered the room demanded an explanation, Sameer stepped forward calmly and took full responsibility for the accident. He accepted the penalty and community service without uttering a single word of complaint. Later, under the shade of the old banyan tree, Rohan confronted Sameer, asking why he had ruined his own spotless record. Sameer smiled gently and replied, 'You have a scholarship to protect, Rohan. Friends stand by each other when it matters most.' Tears filled Rohan's eyes as he embraced his true friend.

  1. Guarding the Precious Cargo

Ramdeen, an old homeless man, lived near the bustling railway station, accompanied everywhere by his faithful stray dog, Moti. Despite having very little, Ramdeen shared his daily bread with Moti, and the two shared an unbreakable bond of loyalty.

One chilly winter evening, as dusk settled over the platform, Moti began barking frantically near a pile of unattended cardboard boxes behind a tea stall. Ramdeen hurried over and was astonished to find a sleeping baby wrapped tightly in a yellow shawl, abandoned amidst the cold wind.

While Moti stood guard over the infant, growling fiercely to deter stray animals and curious onlookers, Ramdeen ran straight to the railway police post. The officers rushed to the spot, wrapped the baby in a blanket, and called an ambulance. Thanks to Ramdeen's swift action and Moti's vigilant protection, the baby was rescued safely and placed in the care of a loving adoption home.

  1. Winds of Change

The small riverside village of Palaspur had long been famous for its handcrafted clay pottery. However, with the advent of cheap factory-made plastic goods, the local artisans faced severe financial hardship, and many young people were abandoning their traditional craft to move to big cities.

Seventeen-year-old Ananya, daughter of the master potter, refused to let her ancestral heritage perish. She researched modern eco-friendly trends online and persuaded the village elders to experiment with contemporary designs, glazed cookware, and biodegradable clay jewelry. She also set up a social media page to sell the products directly to buyers across the country.

Within six months, orders began pouring in from major cities. The village workshops buzzed with renewed life, and young artisans returned home to join the thriving cooperative. The winds of change had blown through Palaspur, proving that tradition and innovation together could create a prosperous future.

  1. A Speech to Remember

The school hall was packed for the annual Inter-School Literary Awards. Vikram, a quiet Class VIII student who suffered from a mild stammer, sat nervously in the second row, clutching a crumpled piece of paper. His English teacher, Mrs. D'Souza, had spent months encouraging him to participate in the poetry recitation competition.

When his name was announced, a quiet hush descended upon the audience. Vikram walked to the podium, took a deep breath, and began to speak. As he recited his original poem about overcoming inner fear, his voice grew steady, resonant, and deeply moving. The raw emotion in his delivery held the entire auditorium spellbound.

When he finished, the audience erupted into a standing ovation. Moments later, the chief guest presented Vikram with the Gold Trophy for Best Orator. Holding the shining trophy, Vikram walked down the aisle and handed it to Mrs. D'Souza, tears streaming down his cheeks. 'I just didn't know what to say!'

  1. A New Dawn

As the sun rose on the changed landscape, the valley looked entirely unfamiliar. The violent cloudburst of the previous night had triggered a massive landslide, sweeping away the wooden footbridge and altering the course of the mountain river.

Villagers emerged from the relief shelter, gazing in shock at the mud-caked fields and uprooted trees. However, despair quickly gave way to collective resolve. The village head, Sarpanch Devraj, rallied everyone together on the high ground. 'The land may have changed, but our spirit remains unbroken,' he announced firmly.

By mid-morning, teams of young men and women were clearing river debris, building a temporary rope bridge, and distributing fresh drinking water to families. Neighbor helped neighbor, sharing food stores and rebuilding collapsed fences. As golden sunlight bathed the valley, the community stepped forward together into a new dawn of resilience.

  1. The Forbidden Cupboard

In the dusty attic of his grandmother's colonial bungalow stood a massive mahogany wardrobe known to all as 'The Forbidden Cupboard'. Grandmother had strictly forbidden anyone from opening its carved brass doors, claiming it contained fragile family heirlooms.

During a rainy afternoon, twelve-year-old Leo was searching for a lost badminton racket when his foot brushed against a brass key lying under a rug. Driven by overwhelming curiosity, he inserted the key into the cupboard lock. The doors creaked open, revealing stacks of yellowed journals, leather maps, and a silver compass.

As Leo flipped through the brittle pages of the top diary, he discovered the captivating account of his great-grandfather, who had been a freedom fighter and secret code-breaker during the independence movement. Overwhelmed by pride, Leo realized why his grandmother preserved the cabinet so carefully—it was a sacred shrine to their family's heroic history.

  1. The Floating City

I stepped out of the archway and gasped in wonder. Below me, instead of solid earth, stretched a shimmering sea of pastel clouds dotted with floating crystal towers connected by light bridges. Gravitational laws seemed entirely suspended as people glided effortlessly through the azure sky.

A winged guide named Zephyr offered me a glowing orb that allowed me to soar above the tallest spire. Together, we swooped past waterfalls cascading into mid-air and gardens where glowing flowers hummed soft melodies. It felt like living inside a breathtaking fantasy beyond human imagination.

Suddenly, the sky began to flicker with silver lightning, and a deep rumbling sound vibrated through the air, shaking the floating towers. My heart leaped into my throat as I felt myself falling rapidly through the clouds into the vast blue void. And then I woke up.

  1. Laughter in the Shadows

Jojo had spent forty years bringing smiles to crowds as a circus clown. After retiring, he decided to volunteer at St. Jude's Asylum, a residential psychiatric facility, hoping to bring a ray of light to patients suffering from deep trauma and depression.

Dr. Marcus, the head psychiatrist, was initially skeptical about introducing clowning performance into a medical environment. However, Jojo's gentle demeanor, silent pantomimes, and colorful balloon art slowly broke through barriers that conventional therapies had failed to penetrate. Patients who had not spoken in months began smiling, participating in games, and expressing emotions freely.

Dr. Marcus watched in amazement during a afternoon session as a deeply withdrawn patient laughed aloud while learning to juggle foam balls with Jojo. Recognizing the profound healing power of joy, Dr. Marcus officially integrated performance arts therapy into the asylum's treatment program, proving that compassion and laughter are potent medicine.

writing.title: Formal Email Writing
writing.html:
📌 What is a Formal Email?

A formal email is the electronic equivalent of a formal letter. It is used for official communication with school principals, teachers, business managers, or authorities. Because emails are read quickly, the language must be extremely concise, clear, and professional.

📝 Format / Structure (Word Limit: 100-120 words)

The format is enclosed in a BOX to simulate a computer screen/email client: 

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Date    : 24 May 2026                                                       |
| From    : student.name@email.com                                            |
| To      : principal.school@email.com                                        |
| Cc      : principal.school@email.com                                        |
| Bcc     : principal.school@email.com                                        |
| Subject : Request for extension of project submission deadline.             |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Respected Sir/Madam,                                                        |
|                                                                             |
| Paragraph 1: State the purpose of the email directly.                       |
| Paragraph 2: Provide brief, necessary details or reasons.                   |
| Paragraph 3: State the action required and conclude politely.               |
|                                                                             |
| Regards,                                                                    |
| Name                                                                        |
| Designation/Class                                                           |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

(Note: Some formats also include 'Cc' (Carbon Copy) and 'Bcc' (Blind Carbon Copy) below the 'To' field. Include them if your teacher specifically asks, but Date, From, To, and Subject are the essential headers.)

⚖️ CBSE Marking Scheme (Typically 5 Marks)

  • Format: 1 Mark (Box, headers, salutation, sign-off)
  • Content: 2 Marks (Clarity of purpose, relevant details)
  • Expression: 2 Marks (Polite tone, grammar, brevity)

💡 Language Tips & Key Rules

  • Subject Line: This is the most important part of an email. It must be a short phrase summarizing the email (e.g., Application for sick leave). Do not write a full sentence in the subject line.
  • Brevity: Do not write long, winding stories. Get straight to the point in the first sentence.
  • Tone: Formal and polite. Never use text slang (like 'u', 'pls', 'thx').

⚠️ Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Leaving the subject line blank or writing "Hi" as the subject.
  • Forgetting to draw the box around the email.
  • Using informal sign-offs like "Lots of love" or "Yours lovingly". Always use "Regards," or "Sincerely,".

🌟 Model Example

Q: You are Amit/Amita, the Secretary of the IT Club of your school. Write an email to the Principal of a neighboring school inviting their students to participate in an Inter-School Coding Competition organized by your club. 

+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Date    : 10 October 2026                                                   |
| From    : itclub.dps@email.com                                              |
| To      : principal.modernschool@email.com                                  |
| Cc      : principal.school@email.com                                        |
| Bcc     : principal.school@email.com                                        |
| Subject : Invitation for Inter-School Coding Competition 2026               |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Respected Sir/Madam,                                                        |
|                                                                             |
| I am writing on behalf of the IT Club of Delhi Public School to formally    |
| invite your students to participate in our annual Inter-School Coding       |
| Competition, 'Code-Fest 2026'.                                              |
|                                                                             |
| The event is scheduled to be held on 25th October 2026 in our school        |
| computer labs from 9:00 AM to 2:00 PM. The competition is open to students  |
| of Classes IX and X. We believe this platform will provide a great          |
| opportunity for young tech enthusiasts to showcase their programming skills.|
|                                                                             |
| We have attached the detailed brochure and registration forms with this     |
| email. We kindly request you to forward this to your Computer Science       |
| department. The last date for registration is 18th October.                 |
|                                                                             |
| We look forward to enthusiastic participation from your esteemed school.    |
|                                                                             |
| Regards,                                                                    |
| Amit Sharma                                                                 |
| Secretary, IT Club, DPS                                                     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

✍️ Practice Prompts

  1. Write a formal email to the Manager of an electronics store inquiring about the bulk pricing of 20 tablets for your school's digital library.
  2. Write an email to your class teacher submitting your Science project online and apologizing for a one-day delay due to internet issues at home.

writing.title: Essay Writing
writing.html:
An essay is a foray into the imagination; it is a work expressing our opinions, thoughts and understanding of a topic or a theme. Like all works of composition, an essay, too, has a format. The usual format of an essay is that it is divided into paragraphs.

The opening paragraph of an essay is normally called the introduction. The last or final paragraph is called the conclusion. In between the introduction and the conclusion, there may be one or more paragraphs that constitute the body of the composition. These paragraphs help to develop the thoughts and ideas to be expressed in the composition.

Let us recapitulate the qualities of a good composition.
- An essay must have unity of thought, that is, it should focus on one definite theme.
- It should follow an order or sequence and have a logical flow.
- The length of an essay ought to be around three hundred words.
- The composition should be written in a simple style.
- The composition must reveal the personal feelings and opinions of the writer. Without the personal touch, a composition becomes devoid of individuality.

NOTE:
In order to write a good essay, it helps to spend a few moments writing down the questions that arise in your mind after seeing the topic, and trying to answer them.
Start the composition with the help of a creative introduction. You may use one of the various methods given below—
- by setting the scene for the story
- by plunging straight into action
- by an interesting or unusual detail
- by a dialogue
Make sure you end the essay with a meaningful conclusion. Remember to round off your narration and avoid ending your composition with sentences such as 'In conclusion...', 'It can be seen that...', 'Summing up, I'd like to state...'.

A. Write essays of about 300 words on any three topics from the ones listed below.
1. Your City on a Festive Evening
2. Recess at School
3. The India of Your Dreams
4. Your Favourite Fictional Character
5. Your First Outing Without Your Parents
6. A Terrifying Experience
7. A Day in the Life of a Stray Dog

B. Write an essay of about 300 words on these situations.
1. Imagine you are an alien who has just arrived on earth from another planet. You are shocked by the amount of waste you see. Write a description of the specific scenes that shock you.
2. Imagine that you have been granted three wishes. What would you wish for and why? Justify the order of priority.
3. What you would do to make the world a happier place to live in?

Answers – Essay Writing

Exercise A

Topic 1: Your City on a Festive Evening

As dusk descends upon the city on the eve of Diwali, a magical transformation unfolds. The grey concrete structures and bustling streets, usually consumed by the relentless noise of daily traffic, dissolve into a shimmering canvas of light and colour. Every balcony, doorway, and rooftop glows with the warm, golden flicker of earthen diyas and intricate strings of fairy lights. The air carries a crisp fragrance of jasmine garlands, burning incense, and sweet delicacies being prepared in neighbourhood kitchens.

Walking through the market square is an immersive sensory experience. Hawkers line the pavements, their stalls overflowing with vibrant marigold flowers, festive decorations, and colorful rangoli powders. Families dressed in their finest traditional attire stroll leisurely, greeting neighbors with joy and exchanged boxes of sweets. Children run through open courtyards with sparklers in hand, tracing glowing arcs against the darkening sky. The distant crackle of firecrackers echoes rhythmically, weaving together with laughter and cheerful chatter.

The festive evening brings a profound sense of unity and warmth to urban life. Differences dissolve as people open their hearts and homes to share blessings. As the night deepens, the city stands illuminated, radiant with hope, harmony, and unbridled happiness.

Topic 2: Recess at School

The ringing of the recess bell at 11:30 a.m. is undoubtedly the most eagerly awaited moment of the school day. In an instant, the quiet discipline of the classroom gives way to a joyous roar as hundreds of students spill into the corridors and playground. The school environment instantly springs to life with energy, laughter, and high-spirited activity.

The playground transforms into a chaotic hive of recreation. In one corner, a lively game of football begins spontaneously with an old tennis ball, while near the assembly stage, girls gather in animated circles to share stories and snacks. The canteen line is perpetually buzzing as students rush to get hot snacks. Shared tiffin boxes reveal a colorful array of sandwiches, noodles, and home-cooked treats, fostering a sense of camaraderie that no lesson plan can replicate.

All too soon, the sharp toll of the bell signals the end of the twenty-minute respite. Dusting off their uniforms, students reluctantly head back to their classrooms, energized and refreshed. Recess is not merely a break from academic rigor; it is the beating heart of school life where lifelong friendships are nurtured.

Topic 3: The India of Your Dreams

The India of my dreams is a sovereign, prosperous, and harmonious nation where every citizen lives with dignity, equality, and peace. It is a land where ancient cultural heritage seamlessly blends with modern technological progress, creating a society that respects its past while courageously forging ahead into the future.

In this visionary nation, education and healthcare are accessible to every child, regardless of socio-economic background. No child is forced into labour, and no youth is deprived of opportunities to excel. Agriculture is modernized to ensure prosperity for our farmers, while sustainable industries protect our precious natural environment. Diversity of language, religion, and culture remains our greatest strength, celebrated with tolerance and mutual respect.

Ultimately, the India of my dreams is free from the shackles of poverty, corruption, and social discrimination. It stands as a global beacon of peace, innovation, and humanitarian values, fulfilling the aspirations of every citizen.

Exercise B

Situation 1: An Alien's Perspective on Earth's Waste

Hovering in my cloak-shielded vessel above the third planet from the sun, my sensors recorded alarming anomalies. Descending toward a dense urban hub, I anticipated witnessing advanced planetary care from a civilization that calls itself intelligent. Instead, I was profoundly shocked by the overwhelming piles of discarded matter smothering the terrestrial ecosystem.

Giant mountains of synthetic non-biodegradable polymer—what Earthlings call 'plastic'—choked waterways and smothered once-fertile soil. I observed pristine oceans polluted with discarded containers, trapping marine life in toxic tangles. In city centers, heaps of food waste lay rotting beside glittering glass towers, emitting foul gases while hungry creatures scavenged nearby. The atmosphere was heavy with acrid smoke from burning refuse heaps, suffocating the very air the inhabitants breathe.

It is terrifying to witness a species squandering its natural sanctuary with such reckless disregard. If Earthlings do not immediately alter their consumption habits and adopt closed-loop recycling, their beautiful planet will soon collapse under the weight of their own waste.

Situation 2: Three Wishes Granted

If a benevolent force were to grant me three wishes today, I would select them with deep reflection, prioritizing global well-being over personal indulgence.

My first priority wish would be the eradication of all incurable diseases and global pandemics. Health is the foundation of human existence; freeing humanity from physical suffering would restore hope and joy to millions of families across the world.

My second wish would be the complete restoration of Earth's natural climate and ecosystems. I would wish for polluted rivers to run clear, endangered species to thrive, and forests to flourish once more, reversing environmental damage.

My final wish would be the universal access to quality education for every child on Earth. Education empowers minds, eradicates prejudice, and equips future generations to solve complex challenges peacefully.

Situation 3: Making the World a Happier Place

Making the world a happier place does not necessarily require grand political movements; it begins with intentional, compassionate actions in our daily lives. To create a happier world, I would focus on fostering empathy, active kindness, and community connection.

First, I would initiate community support circles in neighborhoods to ensure no elderly or lonely individual feels isolated. Simple acts like listening attentively and offering help build strong emotional bonds. Second, I would promote environmental stewardship by organizing tree-planting drives and neighborhood cleanups, as living in clean, green surroundings directly enhances mental well-being.

Finally, I would advocate for kindness education in schools, teaching children emotional intelligence, gratitude, and peaceful conflict resolution. When we cultivate compassion in young minds, we plant the seeds for a peaceful, harmonious world.

writing.title: Article Writing
writing.html:
📌 What is an Article?

An article is a comprehensive piece of writing published in newspapers or school magazines. In Class IX, an article expects a mature analysis of a topic—usually a social issue, environmental concern, or a teenage-centric problem. It must present a balanced view, including causes, effects, and pragmatic solutions.

📝 Format / Structure (Word Limit: 120-150 words)

  1. Title/Heading: Centered, catchy, and relevant. (Capitalize main words).
  2. Byline: Just below the title on the right (e.g., By Amit, Class IX-A).
  3. Paragraph 1 (Introduction - The Hook):
    - Start with a striking fact, a quote, or a rhetorical question.
    - Introduce the topic and its current relevance.
  4. Paragraph 2 (Body - Analysis):
    - Causes: Why is this issue happening?
    - Effects: How does it impact society, students, or the environment?
    - Include statistics or real-life examples to strengthen your point.
  5. Paragraph 3 (Conclusion - The Solution):
    - Suggest practical, actionable solutions.
    - Conclude with a strong, thought-provoking sentence or a call to action.

⚖️ CBSE Marking Scheme (Typically 5-8 Marks)

  • Format (Title + Byline): 1 Mark
  • Content (Ideas, logic, relevance): 3-4 Marks
  • Expression (Grammatical accuracy, mature vocabulary, cohesion): 2-3 Marks

💡 Language Tips & Key Rules

  • Formal Tone: Do not use slang, abbreviations, or conversational language.
  • Linkers / Connectors: Use words like Furthermore, consequently, paradoxically, inevitably, therefore to connect your sentences smoothly.
  • Third Person Perspective: Generally, use the third person ("It is evident that..."). You can use "we" in the conclusion when calling for collective action.

⚠️ Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Writing the article without paragraphs. It MUST be broken into Intro, Body, and Conclusion.
  • Providing problems without suggesting any solutions at the end.
  • Straying away from the given topic.

🌟 Model Example

Q: You are Rohan/Riya. Write an article for your school magazine on the topic: "The Menace of Cyberbullying Among Teenagers."

The Menace of Cyberbullying Among Teenagers
By Riya

The digital age has brought the world to our fingertips, but it has also unleashed a silent, invisible monster: cyberbullying. With the exponential rise in the use of social media among teenagers, the internet has unfortunately become a breeding ground for harassment and intimidation.

Unlike traditional bullying, cyberbullying does not stop at the school gates; it follows the victim home. Hiding behind the veil of anonymity, bullies use fake profiles to post derogatory comments, spread malicious rumors, or share embarrassing photographs. The consequences are devastating. Victims often suffer from severe anxiety, depression, and a steep decline in academic performance. In extreme cases, it leads to tragic outcomes like self-harm.

Eradicating this menace requires a collective effort. Parents and teachers must cultivate an environment where teenagers feel safe discussing their online experiences without fear of losing their internet privileges. Furthermore, schools should conduct regular awareness workshops on cyber ethics. As responsible netizens, teenagers must learn to block and report toxic behavior, ensuring the internet remains a space for learning, not torment.

✍️ Practice Prompts

  1. Write an article on "The Importance of Mental Health Awareness in Schools." Highlight how academic pressure affects students and what can be done.
  2. Write an article on "Water Scarcity: The Looming Crisis." Detail the causes and the urgent need for water conservation.

writing.title: Informal Letter
writing.html:
📌 What is an Informal Letter?

An informal letter is a personal letter written to friends, family members, or relatives to share personal news, express feelings, ask for advice, or describe an experience. At the Class IX level, the letter should display emotional depth, mature vocabulary, and well-structured paragraphs despite the casual tone.

📝 Format / Structure (Word Limit: 120-150 words)

The format follows a left-aligned layout:

  1. Sender’s Address: Top left corner.
  2. Date: Below the address (e.g., 24 May 2026).
  3. Salutation: E.g., Dear Rahul, Dear Mom,
  4. Body of the Letter:
    - Paragraph 1 (Introduction): Inquire about their health and state the reason for writing the letter.
    - Paragraph 2 (Main Content): Expand on the topic. Give vivid details of the experience, problem, or news you are sharing. Show your feelings.
    - Paragraph 3 (Conclusion): Concluding remarks, hopes for a reply, and sending love to other family members.
  5. Subscription: Yours lovingly, / Yours affectionately,
  6. Name: First name only.

⚖️ CBSE Marking Scheme (Typically 5-8 Marks)

  • Format: 1-2 Marks (Address, Date, Salutation, Closing)
  • Content: 3-4 Marks (Relevance, ideas, elaboration)
  • Expression: 2 Marks (Grammar, vocabulary, friendly but mature tone)

💡 Language Tips & Key Phrases

  • Opening:
  • "I was delighted to read your last letter..."
  • "I hope this letter finds you in the pink of health."
  • Tone: Conversational and warm. You can use contractions (I've, couldn't, haven't).
  • Elaboration: Don't just state facts. If you went on a trip, describe how it made you feel.

⚠️ Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Using formal sign-offs: Never use "Yours faithfully" or "Yours sincerely" in an informal letter.
  • Missing the Date: Ensure the date is written in the correct format (15 May 2026, not 15/05/26).

🌟 Model Example

Q: You are Sneha/Sumit studying in a boarding school in Dehradun. Write a letter to your mother telling her about your experience of participating in a grueling 3-day adventure camp organized by the school.

Room No. 42, Ganga Hostel
Doon Public School
Dehradun

12 October 2026

Dear Mom,

I hope you and dad are doing wonderful back home. I am writing this letter to share my thrilling experience at the 3-day adventure camp our school organized in Rishikesh last weekend.

Honestly, mom, when I first saw the itinerary, I was terrified. The camp included rock climbing, valley crossing, and white-water rafting. On the first day during the rock climbing session, my hands were shaking, and I almost gave up halfway. However, our instructor and my friends cheered me on, and when I finally reached the top, the feeling of accomplishment was indescribable! The river rafting the next day was the highlight—the freezing water splashing against our faces was both scary and exhilarating.

This trip pushed me out of my comfort zone and taught me that I am much stronger than I thought. I can't wait to show you all the photographs during the winter break.

Give my love to dad and little Rohan. Miss you all!

Yours lovingly,
Sneha

✍️ Practice Prompts

  1. Write a letter to your friend apologizing for your rude behavior during an argument last week, and asking for their forgiveness.
  2. You recently read a highly inspiring book. Write a letter to your cousin recommending the book to them and explaining why you liked it so much.

writing.title: Informal Invitation Letter
writing.html:
📌 What is an Informal Invitation Letter?

An informal invitation letter is written to invite friends, relatives, or close acquaintances to personal events such as a birthday party, an anniversary, a housewarming, or a casual get-together. The tone is warm, personal, and friendly, completely avoiding official jargon.

📝 Format / Structure (Word Limit: 50-100 words)

The format is similar to a regular informal letter but is usually shorter and more direct.

  1. Sender’s Address: Top left corner.
  2. Date: Below the address (e.g., 24 May 2026).
  3. Salutation: Dear [First Name],
  4. Body of the Letter:
    - The Invite: Clearly state what the occasion is and explicitly invite the person.
    - The Details: Mention the Date, Time, and Venue of the event clearly.
    - Personal Touch: Add a line about how much their presence would mean to you or what fun activities are planned.
  5. Subscription (Closing): Yours lovingly, / Yours affectionately,
  6. Sender’s Name: First name only.

⚖️ CBSE Marking Scheme (Typically 3-4 Marks)

  • Format: 1 Mark
  • Content (Occasion, Date, Time, Venue): 1-2 Marks
  • Expression (Friendly tone, grammar): 1 Mark

💡 Language Tips & Useful Phrases

  • Opening phrases:
  • "I am thrilled to invite you to..."
  • "You will be glad to know that..."
  • "It gives me immense pleasure to invite you and your family to..."
  • Adding warmth:
  • "The party won't be the same without you."
  • "Looking forward to celebrating together."

⚠️ Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Forgetting Event Details: An invitation is useless if you forget to mention when and where it is happening.
  • Using formal language: Do not use "Respected" or "Yours faithfully."
  • Writing too much: Unlike a regular informal letter where you discuss life and health at length, an invitation should get straight to the point.

🌟 Model Example

Q: You are Ankit/Ankita. You are organizing a surprise 50th birthday party for your father. Write an informal letter inviting your uncle, who lives in Chandigarh, to the party.

14, Green Park
New Delhi

15 October 2026

Dear Uncle Suresh,

I hope you and Aunt are doing well. You will be glad to know that dad is turning 50 next week. To celebrate this milestone, mom and I are organizing a surprise birthday party for him.

It gives me immense pleasure to invite you and Aunt to the celebration. The party will be held at our residence on Sunday, 25th October 2026, starting at 7:00 PM. We have arranged for dad's favorite live music band and a wonderful dinner.

Since it is a surprise, please do not mention it to dad when you speak to him! The celebration will be incomplete without your presence. We are eagerly waiting to see you.

Yours lovingly,
Ankit

✍️ Practice Prompts

  1. Write an informal letter to your best friend inviting them to your house for a weekend pajama party to celebrate the end of your final exams. Mention the date and activities planned.
  2. Your family has just moved into a new apartment. Write an informal letter to your cousin inviting them to the housewarming ceremony.

Let us read

Word Meaning

illustrious respected and famous
patron supporter
eminent famous

The Vijayanagara Empire was renowned for its glory, wealth, and cultural achievements. Among its many illustrious rulers, King Krishnadeva Raya (ruled 1509–29 CE) stood out as a wise and powerful monarch. His reign is often referred to as the Golden Era of the Vijayanagara Empire, a time when art, literature, and architecture flourished. A great patron of learning, Krishnadeva Raya was not only an eminent warrior but also a gifted poet. His works, such as the epic Amuktamalyada and the Sanskrit drama Jambavati Parinayam, are acclaimed even today.

Krishnadeva Raya’s court was home to eight celebrated poets, collectively known as the Ashtadiggajas. These poets, including Allasani Peddana and Tenali Ramakrishna, enriched the literary tradition with their masterpieces. Tenali Ramakrishna, in particular, was known for his quick wit and humour, earning him a special place in the king’s court as both a poet and a witty advisor. His clever solutions to seemingly insurmountable problems made him a beloved figure in the empire’s history.

Even the wisest rulers face moments of disharmony, and at one such time, the king had a quarrel with his queen, Thirumalambal, over a seemingly trivial matter. For weeks, he did not utter a single word to her, and in his frustration, stopped visiting her altogether. His absence cast a shadow over the palace, and the once cheerful corridors seemed quiet and forlorn.

Thirumalambal, distraught and upset, tried her best to resolve the issue but failed. With no other alternative, she decided to seek the help of Tenali Rama, the court’s brilliant and witty poet. Rama listened patiently as the queen recounted the incident in detail.

Word Meaning
insurmountable undefeatable
trivial unimportant
forlorn lonely
distraught upset
vague unclear

“The king wrote a poem,” she began, her voice trembling. “It was filled with vague expressions—sun, moon, stars, beautiful sky—but it made no sense. When he tried reciting it to his ministers, they all avoided him, making excuses. It was late evening when he came to me, seeking an audience. He began reciting it to me, but I was so exhausted after a tiring day that I yawned— not once, but several times. The king thought I was disrespecting his poem and stormed off. Since then, he has not spoken to me. If I had known this would happen I would have chosen another day. Help me, please, Rama. Only you can help the king understand.”

Word Meaning
strategy plan
profusely in large amounts
bustling busy
intricately in a detailed manner
exquisite fine and attractive
ornate decorative
gnawed (here) bothered

Rama nodded thoughtfully. “If you like, I will try my best to resolve this matter, Your Highness. But this needs a well-planned approach, and I may need time to find the right strategy.” The queen, who had placed her last hope in Rama, agreed and thanked him profusely.

The next morning, the royal court was bustling with activity. Ministers, scholars, and courtiers filled the courtroom, its intricately carved pillars towering towards the high ceiling. Rays of sunlight streamed through the open windows, illuminating the floor adorned with exquisite rugs. Despite the lively chatter, a tension hung in the air. The king sat on his ornate throne, his expression stern, his sharp eyes scanning the room. It was evident that the unresolved quarrel still gnawed at him.

The court discussion was centred on improving paddy cultivation in the empire. One by one, the ministers rose to present their ideas. Some suggested expanding irrigation networks, while others advocated for better manure. Amid these suggestions, Tenali Rama stood quietly at the edge of the court, observing everyone with an amused smile.

Finally, the king called upon Rama. The chatter in the court died down as all eyes turned to him. Rama approached the throne, carrying a plateful of paddy seeds. Bowing low, he began, “Your Majesty, I bring you a revolutionary type of paddy seeds. If these are sown, the yield will be three times greater than the current results.”

A murmur swept through the room. One of the courtiers, known for his sarcasm, whispered just loud enough to be heard, “I wonder if these are magic seeds! Next, he’ll claim they grow without water.” Another muttered, “Perhaps he found them on the moon!” Snickers rippled through the court.

The king frowned, unimpressed. “That sounds absurd,” he muttered. “Such cultivation would need special soil, manure, and pest and insect repellents. If, by chance, something were to go wrong, our farmers would suffer.”

Rama smiled, unfazed. “That may be true, Your Majesty, but the real issue lies not with the seeds themselves but with the person who sows them.”

Word Meaning
yield harvest
sarcasm mockery
snickers suppressed laughter
absurd illogical
unfazed not worried
furrowed wrinkled
sceptical doubtful
keenly intensely
gesture a movement of a hand or the head, to express an idea or a meaning
A hush fell over the court as Rama’s words hung in the air. The king’s eyebrows furrowed. “What is wrong with the person who sows the seeds? Speak clearly, Rama!” he roared.

Rama glanced around the court, his sharp gaze meeting the sceptical eyes of the courtiers. “If one were to sow seeds without proper care, no one would reap a good harvest,” he said, pausing for effect. “And what if the person had a habit of yawning while sowing? Wouldn’t the seeds scatter unevenly?”

The court erupted into laughter, the earlier sarcasm replaced by genuine amusement. Even the king, caught off guard, sighed and instinctively yawned. Rama watched him keenly, then continued, “Your Majesty, is there anyone in this world who does not yawn? It is as natural as breathing.”

The king’s expression shifted as realisation dawned. His mind raced back to the quarrel with the queen. He remembered scolding her harshly for yawning while he recited his poem. He realised how unfair he had been. “If I had known that yawning was not a sign of disrespect, I wouldn’t have taken her gesture so personally,” he thought, regret filling his heart.

That evening, the king approached the queen with a softened expression. “Thirumalambal,” he began, his voice gentle, “I have been foolish. I see now that I overreacted. I let my pride blind me. I’m so sorry.”

The queen, who had longed for this moment, smiled and replied, “If you like, we can leave this quarrel behind us. I would very much like to listen to your poem.”

Rama, who had orchestrated this settlement, felt victorious. The king and the queen later presented him with valuable gifts for his service. The royal couple’s bond was restored, and the palace brimmed once again with joy and laughter.

Word Meaning

One bright Monday morning, I woke up to the sounds of birds chirping loudly. For once, I wasn't late for school. My uniform was neatly laid out, and my homework was already packed in my bag. literature.title: A Concrete Example
literature.html:
Let us read

My next-door neighbour, Mrs. Jones,
has got a garden full of stones:
A crazy path, a lily pond,
a rockery and, just beyond
A sundial with a strange device,
which Mrs. Jones thinks rather nice.

My next-door neighbour, Mrs. Jones,
puts little plants between the stones
They are so delicate and small,
they don't mean anything at all.
I can't think how she gets them in,
unless she plants them with a pin.

My next-door neighbour, Mrs. Jones,
once asked me round to see her stones.
We stood and talked about a flower
for quite a quarter of an hour.
"Where is this lovely thing?" I cried.
"You're standing on it," she replied.

REGINALD ARKELL

Summary

The poem humorously describes Mrs. Jones, the speaker's next-door neighbour, who is passionate about her peculiar garden full of stones. Her garden includes a "crazy path," a lily pond, a rockery, and a sundial with a strange device. She plants tiny, delicate plants between the stones — so small the speaker jokes they could be planted with a pin. When Mrs. Jones invites the speaker to admire a flower, the speaker discovers they have been standing on it the whole time. The poem is a light-hearted commentary on different perceptions of beauty and the irony of overlooking what is right in front of us.

Poetic Devices

  • Refrain — "My next-door neighbour, Mrs. Jones" is repeated at the start of each stanza, anchoring the poem's structure.

  • Irony — The situational irony of the speaker standing on the very flower they are admiring creates a humorous twist.

  • Pun — The title "A Concrete Example" works literally (concrete/stones in the garden) and figuratively (a clear illustration of Mrs. Jones's gardening habits).

  • Hyperbole — "They don't mean anything at all" and "planted them with a pin" exaggerate the speaker's dismissiveness.

  • Imagery — "A crazy path, a lily pond, a rockery" and "delicate and small" plants create vivid visual pictures of the garden.

  • Enjambment — Lines flow into each other without punctuation breaks, maintaining a conversational, anecdotal pace.

  • Anticlimax — The build-up of describing Mrs. Jones's garden leads to the anticlimactic reveal that the speaker has been standing on the flower — the grand moment is deflated for comic effect.

  • Understatement — "They don't mean anything at all" understates the speaker's ignorance, making the irony sharper.

  • Tone: Humorous, light-hearted, and gently mocking.

Rhyme Scheme

ABBACC — each stanza follows this six-line pattern (e.g., Jones/stones/pond/beyond/device/nice).

literature.html:
Let us read

I.

Encyclopedia Brown is a young boy who lives in Idaville, USA. His father is the Chief of Police. In spite of being so young he often helps his father solve mysteries that even the police find difficult to solve. Their discussions are generally held at the dining table. Read this story to find out how the boy wonder solves a case that has been troubling his father...

Encyclopedia’s father was Chief of Police. Everyone thought that he must be the smartest police chief in the country. Chief Brown was smart and quick. He didn’t sit around and worry. When he came up against a case he couldn’t solve, he acted at once. He cleared his desk, put on his hat, and went home to dinner. Encyclopedia solved the case for him before dinner was over.

Chief Brown would have liked to tell everyone about his only child. But who would believe him? Who would believe that the best detective alive was an eighth grader? So, he said nothing.

Encyclopedia never spoke of the help he gave his father. He didn’t want to seem different from other boys. But there was nothing he could do about his nickname. He was stuck with it.

Only his parents and teachers called him by his real name, Leroy. Everyone else called him Encyclopedia.

An encyclopedia is a book or set of books filled with facts from A to Z. So was Encyclopedia’s head. He read more books than anyone in Idaville, and he never forgot a fact. His pals said he was like a library and computer rolled into one, and more user-friendly.

Word Meaning
nickname pet name

At the dinner table on Tuesday night, Chief Brown stared at his cream-of-mushroom soup. Encyclopedia and his mother knew what that meant. He had a mystery he could not solve.

“Tim Nolan died yesterday,” he announced in a matter-of-fact manner.

“That name is familiar,” Mrs. Brown said. “Wasn’t he mixed up in a jewellery robbery a few years ago?”

“Five years ago,” Chief Brown replied. “Two masked men held up the Diamond Mart on Sixth Avenue. They got away with a million dollars worth of jewellery.”

“I thought Tim Nolan was arrested,” Mrs. Brown said.

“He was questioned, not arrested,” Chief Brown corrected.

“I always believed that Nolan and a friend, a man named Daniel Davenport, pulled the hold-ups. There wasn’t any proof, though.”

Encyclopedia sat quietly. He knew his mother and father were discussing the case for his benefit.

His father filled in the facts.

“Nolan and Davenport had met,” Chief Brown said, “while both were in prison in South Carolina. They became friendly because of shared interests.

Nolan was let out first.

He settled in Idaville and started a small palm-tree nursery. It barely yielded him a living.”

“Davenport came to live with Nolan a week before the jewellery store hold-up. During the hold-up, one gunman's mask slipped. A clerk thought she recognised Nolan. But she wasn't absolutely sure."

Word Meaning
in a matter-of-fact manner without showing much emotion
hold-ups robberies conducted with the use of threat or violence
nursery a place where young plants and trees are grown for sale
testify make a statement in court to prove that something is true
hunch a strong feeling about something
loot stolen goods
stroke a sudden serious illness causing inability to move

"I remember now," Mrs. Brown said. "The clerk refused to testify against him, and no trace of the stolen jewellery ever turned up."

"Davenport hasn't been seen since the hold-up," Chief Brown said. "My hunch is that he and Nolan decided to hide the loot until things cooled down."

"Didn't you search Nolan's house, dear?"

"I got a court order this morning," Chief Brown said. "Officers Lewis and Maloney just about took Nolan's house apart. They didn't find one piece of the stolen jewellery."

"Is there some mystery about Nolan's death yesterday?" Mrs. Brown inquired.

"Yes and no," Chief Brown answered. "Nolan suffered from a bad heart for many years. Yesterday morning he had a stroke. He must have realised he was dying. With his last strength, he managed to put his will on the kitchen table. It leaves everything he owns, including his palm-tree nursery to Davenport."

Let us discuss

I. Complete the following statements with suitable reasons. Share your answers with your classmates and teacher.
1. Leroy's nickname was Encyclopedia and everyone called him by that name because _________.
2. At the dinner table on Tuesday night, Chief Brown stared at his cream-of-mushroom soup as _________.
3. Encyclopedia sat quietly at the dinner table because _________.
4. Nolan put the will on the kitchen table because _________.

II. Do you think Chief Brown would need Leroy's help to solve this case? If yes, why? If no, why not?

II.

“What’s suspicious about that?” Mrs. Brown asked.

“Nothing about the will itself—just about a sheet from his desk calendar. It was clipped to the will,” said Chief Brown.

He took out his pocket notebook and leafed through the pages.

“I copied what Nolan wrote on the sheet,” he said. “Here it is.”

He handed the notebook to Mrs. Brown.

She read what he had copied. “It has Davenport’s name and address,” she said, “and a few words I don’t understand.”

She handed the notebook to Encyclopedia.

“What do you make of the four words, Leroy?”

Encyclopedia read the four words below Davenport’s name and address: Nom Utes Sweden Hurts.

Mrs. Brown looked at him hopefully. Usually he needed to ask only one question to solve a case before dessert.

They were still on the soup.

Encyclopedia leaned back and closed his eyes when he did his hardest thinking.

After several seconds, he opened his eyes and asked his question. “Is there a young fir tree in Mr. Nolan’s palm-tree nursery?” Chief Brown thought a moment. “Yes, there is... one. On the south side of the house. How did you know?”

“The four words say so,” Encyclopedia answered.

“They do?” said Chief Brown.

“See for yourself,” Encyclopedia urged.

Chief Brown studied the four words: Nom Utes Sweden Hurts. He shook his head and passed the notebook to Mrs. Brown again. “Can you figure it out?”

Word Meaning
will (here) a legal document that says what is to happen to somebody’s money and property after their death
leafed through quickly turned (the pages)
confessed admitted

“Nom is a shortening of nominative, a grammatical term,” stated Mrs. Brown, who had taught English and other subjects in high school. “Utes are an American Indian tribe. Sweden is a country in northern Europe. Hurts is hurts.”

She lifted her gaze to Encyclopedia and shook her head.

“I can’t figure it out,” she confessed.

“Davenport disappeared right after the hold-up,” Encyclopedia reminded her.

“As Dad said, Davenport and Nolan must have hidden the stolen jewellery. Probably not a week or so ago, Nolan changed the hiding place.”

“You think that he tried to tell Davenport by phone and failed to reach him?” Mrs. Brown asked. “So he wrote the four words as he was dying?”

Chief Brown nodded. “We’ll find Davenport now that we know his address.”

“He’ll learn he has been left the palm-tree nursery,” Mrs. Brown said. “And the four words will tell him where the jewellery is hidden!”

“Right,” Encyclopedia said. “The code is simple, especially as it’s written on a sheet from a calendar. Davenport will understand it easily. Still, it wouldn’t make much sense to someone who isn’t looking for a hiding place.”

“Leroy!” Mrs. Brown exclaimed. “What do the four words mean?”

“You already guessed, Mom. They tell where the jewellery is hidden.”

Mrs. Brown looked ready to explode with impatience, “Where?”

Encyclopedia smiled.

“Why, under the fifth word,” he said.

What Was The Fifth Word?

Word Meaning
code hidden message

To tell Davenport where he had hidden the stolen jewellery, Nolan wrote a four-word code.

As the key to the code, he wrote the four words on a sheet from a desk calendar.

The four words stood for days of the week.

Nolan dropped the letters d-a-y. Then he used the other letters to form words.

So, Nom = Monday, Utes = Tuesday, Sweden = Wednesday and Hurts = Thursday.

The unwritten fifth word was Fir, or Friday.

The jewellery was found inside a twenty-gallon jug of earth from which grew the young fir tree in Nolan’s nursery—just as Encyclopedia had foreseen.

DONALD J. SOBOL
(ADAPTED)

Let us read

The woman was old and ragged and grey
And bent with the chill of the Winter’s day.

The street was wet with a recent snow
And the woman’s feet were aged and slow.

She stood at the crossing and waited long,
Alone, uncared for, amid the throng

Of human beings who passed her by
Nor heeded the glance of her anxious eyes.

Down the street, with laughter and shout,
Glad in the freedom of “school let out,”

Came the boys like a flock of sheep,
Hailing the snow piled white and deep.

Past the woman so old and grey
Hastened the children on their way.

Nor offered a helping hand to her—
So meek, so timid, afraid to stir

Lest the carriage wheels or the horses’ feet
Should crowd her down in the slippery street.

At last came one of the merry troop,
The gayest laddie of all the group;

He paused beside her and whispered low,
“I’ll help you cross, if you wish to go.”

Her aged hand on his strong young arm
She placed, and so, without hurt or harm,

He guided the trembling feet along,
Proud that his own were firm and strong.

Then back again to his friends he went,
His young heart happy and well content.

“She’s somebody’s mother, boys, you know,
For all she’s aged and poor and slow”,

“And I hope some fellow will lend a hand
To help my mother, you understand”,

“If ever she’s poor and old and grey,
When her own dear boy is far away.”

And “somebody’s mother” bowed low her head
In her home that night, and the prayer she said

Was “God be kind to the noble boy,
Who is somebody’s son, and pride and joy!”

MARY DOW BRINE

Summary

On a cold winter day, an old, ragged woman stands alone at a street crossing, too afraid to cross the slippery road. Schoolboys rush past her without a thought, but one kind boy pauses, offers his help, and safely guides her across. He returns to his friends, explaining that she is "somebody's mother" and hoping that someone would do the same for his own mother someday. That night, the old woman prays for the noble boy. The poem celebrates kindness, empathy, and the golden rule of treating others as we wish to be treated.

Poetic Devices

  • Simile — "Came the boys like a flock of sheep" compares the rushing schoolboys to a flock, emphasizing their thoughtless, herd-like behavior.

  • Repetition — "Somebody's mother" is repeated to emphasize the woman's identity and evoke empathy.

  • Alliteration — "meek, timid," "slippery street" create rhythmic sound patterns.

  • Imagery — "The street was wet with a recent snow," "the woman's feet were aged and slow" create vivid visual and tactile images of cold and vulnerability.

  • Contrast — The indifference of the crowd vs. the kindness of one boy; the old woman's frailty vs. the boy's strength.

  • Foreshadowing — The boy's hope that "some fellow will lend a hand / To help my mother" foreshadows the moral reciprocity at the poem's heart.

  • Narrative Arc — The poem follows a clear storytelling structure: setting (cold day, old woman), rising action (boys passing by), climax (one boy helps), resolution (woman prays).

  • Pathos — "Alone, uncared for, amid the throng" and "the prayer she said" evoke deep sympathy and emotional resonance.

  • Direct Address — "She's somebody's mother, boys, you know" breaks the narrative to speak directly to the reader, reinforcing the moral.

  • Tone: Sympathetic, hopeful, and morally uplifting.

Rhyme Scheme

AABB — each stanza uses couplet rhymes (e.g., grey/day, snow/slow, long/throng, by/by).

literature.html:
Let us read

Word Meaning
mystifying strange or impossible to explain
spectacle an unusual sight that attracts interest
exotic uncommon
botanical relating to plants
feats tasks difficult to achieve, especially those involving a lot of skill
indigenous native
tangible noticeable

India is home to some of the most mystifying natural phenomena that surprise and spark our imagination.

  1. THE VALLEY OF FLOWERS, UTTARAKHAND

The Valley of Flowers is an eye-catching spectacle with around 600 species of exotic flowers, including orchids, poppies, primulas, marigold, daisies, and anemones. It is a place where nature blooms in its full glory offering an attractive view.

The trek to the valley offers spectacular views of beautiful waterfalls and wild streams. The valley is also home to rare wildlife species like the grey langur, flying squirrel, red fox, lime butterfly, and snow leopard, to name a few.

With a stunning backdrop of the mighty Himalayan ranges, the Valley of Flowers National Park presents an unforgettable experience for visitors. Spread over a huge area in the Chamoli district, the Valley of Flowers National Park is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Between the months of May and October, this area turns into a botanical wonderland!

  1. THE LIVING ROOT BRIDGES, MEGHALAYA

Imagine building a bridge without the use of cement, stones, concrete, etc. Is it possible? The living root bridges are incredible feats of engineering built by the indigenous people of Meghalaya. The living root bridges are one of Meghalaya’s most beautiful tangible UNESCO world heritage sites.

Crossing the many waterways without bridges was difficult for people in the past, during monsoons.

Attempts to use bamboo or wooden bridges across these waterways proved futile as these bridges could not last long in the heavy rains and strong waters. Living root bridges are an innovative and indigenous solution to solve this age-old problem.

They are made of intertwined roots which are a sort of magic, but they aren't imaginary. These bridges have been built for centuries by the indigenous people of the land. It is a naturally built ecosystem of local flora. It also symbolises the relationship and knowledge that the local people have over their region and the cultural significance that it holds for them. Under ideal conditions, a root bridge is thought to be able to persist for hundreds of years. These bridges frequently rise 50 to 100 feet in the air. The state's longest living root bridge is said to be a whopping 175 feet in length. There are approximately 100 or so known living root bridges across different villages.

  1. THE LONAR CRATER LAKE, MAHARASHTRA

The Lonar Crater Lake is a geological wonder, nestled in the town of Lonar in Buldhana district, Maharashtra. It is believed to have been formed thousands of years ago. This ancient landform, consisting of a giant hole, came into existence when a colossal meteorite, blazing at an extremely high speed, crashed into the Earth, leaving behind a stunning mark. It is the only crater in India formed in basaltic rock by a meteorite impact and ranks as the third largest in the world, placing it among the top five largest craters globally.

The crater's perfectly circular depression cradles a unique saline lake at its core, creating a striking visual contrast against the surrounding rugged terrain. This site is a rare and extraordinary blend of celestial impact and terrestrial beauty. The rim of the meteor crater offers a breath-taking spectacle of nature's power and the enduring allure of our planet's ancient past.

Word Meaning
futile useless
intertwined twisted together
persist continue to exist
whopping huge
nestled situated in a half-hidden or sheltered position
colossal extremely large
cradles holds
rugged rough
terrestrial on or related to earth
allure attraction
  1. MAGNETIC HILLS IN LEH DISTRICT, LADAKH

In the travels around Leh-Ladakh, is a fascinating sight which arouses curiosity to no end—the Magnetic Hill, a place where gravity takes a backseat!

Lying at a distance of around 30 km from Leh, the Magnetic

Hill is marked by a yellow signboard which reads ‘The Phenomenon That Defies Gravity’. It also instructs visitors to park vehicles in the box marked with a white point on the road, which is known as the Magnetic Road. When the vehicles are parked at the indicated spot, they begin moving forward at a speed of almost 20km/h. This unusual place creates an optical illusion where vehicles appear to roll uphill, a sight that has left tourists in disbelief for years, caused by the peculiar alignment of surrounding slopes and the horizon line.

  1. GLOWING WATERS OF KERALA

Situated 15 kms from Kerala’s Kochi town, Kumbalangi is a beautiful village with vast green vegetation. In the serene backwaters of Kumbalangi village, one can see magically glowing waters in the night.

This phenomenon is called bioluminescence, and is caused by a high concentration of micro-planktons in the sea, which are small organisms found in marine and freshwater. This beautiful sight has captured the attention of locals as well as tourists, making Kumbalangi an eco-tourism village in India. One can experience the village life in all its beauty and simplicity, and acquaint oneself to their cuisine and culture.

Word Meaning
optical illusion something that tricks your eyes and makes you see it differently from how it really is
serene calm
backwaters a part of a river where the water does not flow
bioluminescence light produced inside the body of a living organism by a chemical reaction
eco-tourism tourism that is responsible towards preserving the environment
acquaint to become familiar with something
  1. THE SUNDARBANS

Can a forest exist in a coastal zone? Yes, they are called mangrove forests, where trees take root under water in the low-oxygen soil. The roots slow down the movement of tidal waters, stabilising the coastline and reducing erosion. The Sundarbans is one such mangrove forest spread over 1,400 kms in West Bengal, lying in the delta of rivers, such as the Ganga, the Brahmaputra, and the Meghna. The name is derived from sundari trees that are plentiful in the area.

The area is also populated by an extensive range of flora and fauna, including many bird species, the majestic Bengal tiger, and other threatened species, such as the estuarine crocodile and the Indian python.

  1. THE INVISIBLE CHANDIPUR BEACH, ODISHA

Have you seen things disappearing in front of your eyes? Well, such things happen at times, when we keep things at some place, and just forget where we have kept them. But, what if there's a sea that disappears?

This happens in Odisha. It is a beach in the Balasore district where one can witness the sea disappearing mysteriously—the Chandipur Beach which is known for its unique feature of playing hide-and-seek with its visitors.

The sea can actually be witnessed disappearing and reappearing. This is because the sea water moves. It retreats by 2–5 km during ebb tide, the duration between the high tide and low tide, and comes back to the shore at the time of high tide. This unusual natural phenomenon keeps on happening daily, where one can actually see the sea, and then watch it disappear in front of their eyes!

Word Meaning
estuarine living in an estuary (an area where a freshwater river meets the ocean)
retreats goes backwards
ebb tide period of time when water flows away from the shore
mystique mystery
enigmatic puzzling
intrigue interest

These awe-inspiring natural wonders of India highlight the mystique of the country’s landscapes, each phenomenon telling its own story of nature’s artistic flair and enigmatic charm. They challenge our understanding of the natural world and captivate our senses. They serve as a reminder of the extraordinary forces that shape our environment, blending scientific intrigue with the magic of folklore.

literature.html:
Let us read

“Go and gather wild beans, Gopi,
Go and fetch some rice.
Go and pluck the mangoes
And bring home something nice.”

Gopi sits beneath the banyan,
A twig is in her hand.
She sits there drawing pictures,
Pictures in the sand.

The winds blow by and sweeps away
The pictures in the sand.

But on a stone there sits a man,
A brush is in his hand.

He looks around. He calls to Gopi.
“Come here!” he whispers. “Hush!
We mustn’t let the village know
About this magic brush.”

He slips the brush into her hand
And tells her to be sure,
“Paint not for the wealthy ones,
But only for the poor.”

“Did you gather wild beans, Gopi?
Did you fetch some rice?
Did you pluck the mangoes
And bring home something nice?”

“No beans, no rice, no mangoes!”
Gopi grins and runs inside.
She paints a bowl of khichdi
and waits,
Until the paint has dried.

“The bowl is full of khichdi, Gopi!”
Into the house the villagers streamed
The young and old all wish to see
The magic brush of dreams.

She paints a muffler for a farmer,
A plough for another man,
A shawl for a grandmother,
And for a girl, a fan.

And soon the news spreads far and wide,
Through forests, fields, and plains,
Until the Zamindar himself
Hears of these magic gains.

“I order you to paint for me,
A fortress tall and grand.
Paint treasures, jewels, and riches rare,
Enough to rule this land.”

Gopi bows and shakes her head.
“My lord, I can’t comply.
I swore to use this magic brush
To help the needy by.”

The Zamindar roars and stamps his foot.
He bellows to his men,
“Seize this brush and seize the girl.
Throw her in the pen!”

Now Gopi waits inside the cell,
Upon a cold mud floor.
Until the Zamindar returns
And shouts through the door.

He holds the brush. He thunders loud,
“Paint my fortress tall!
Paint gold and rubies, emeralds bright,
And you shall leave this hall!”

That night the Zamindar lies in bed,
Dreaming of his gold,
While Gopi paints a winding road,
A horse both strong and bold.

The road leads out of prison gates.
The horse, she swiftly urges
Gopi leaps on and gallops fast,
Through fields and many villages.

“It’s Gopi! It’s Gopi! She’s back again!”
Say the villagers, merry and kind.
But Gopi keeps on painting still,
With the Zamindar’s men following
behind.

She paints a mighty river wide,
Its currents fast and deep.
The Zamindar and all his men
Stop short and cannot leap.

“Now should I paint a beast
To leap and chase you through?
Stop this chase or it will feast
On you, and you and you!”

The Zamindar cries, “No, no, no more!
I’ll leave, I’ll go away!”
He turns and flees; his men behind
Dare not choose to stay.

Now Gopi paints for the village folk,
A feast of sweets and tea.
A courtyard bright, a band to play,
And songs of victory.

ADAPTED FROM A FOLK TALE

Summary

Gopi, a young girl, is tasked with gathering wild beans, rice, and mangoes but instead spends her time drawing pictures in the sand. A mysterious man gives her a magic brush with one rule: paint only for the poor, never for the wealthy. Gopi uses the brush to paint food, clothing, and tools for villagers in need. When the greedy Zamindar demands she paint treasures for him, she refuses and is thrown in prison. That night, she paints a road and a horse that carry her to freedom. The poem celebrates selfless generosity, courage, and the triumph of good over greed.

Poetic Devices

  • Symbolism — The magic brush symbolizes talent, creativity, and the power of art to serve the common good; the Zamindar represents greed and abuse of power.

  • Personification — The brush is given magical life, capable of turning painted objects into reality.

  • Dialogue — Direct speech ("Paint not for the wealthy ones, but only for the poor") drives the moral lesson.

  • Repetition — "Did you gather wild beans, Gopi? / Did you fetch some rice?" repeated to create a rhythmic call-and-response pattern.

  • Contrast — Gopi's selflessness for the poor vs. the Zamindar's selfishness and greed.

  • Alliteration — "paint... poor," "seize... stamp" create rhythmic consonant patterns.

  • Foreshadowing — The mysterious man's instruction to "paint not for the wealthy ones" foreshadows the conflict with the Zamindar.

  • Archetype — Gopi represents the classic folk hero: humble, selfless, and clever; the Zamindar is the greedy antagonist.

  • Onomatopoeia — "Roars," "bellows," "clatter and a clank" mimic the sounds of conflict and escape.

  • Tone: Whimsical, moral, and adventurous.

Rhyme Scheme

Irregular — the poem does not follow a strict rhyme scheme, using free-flowing lines suited to its folk-tale narrative style.

My Adventure with the Flying Scarf

I was a bright red silk scarf, resting peacefully on a wooden clothesline, when a sudden strong gust of wind swept me into the open sky.

My journey began over bustling city streets where I floated past tall buildings and waved at amazed children looking out of windows. Next, the wind carried me toward a peaceful countryside, where I brushed against green treetops and danced alongside wild birds. I even landed briefly on a cold park bench, offering warmth to an elderly man before the wind gently lifted me once again.

Eventually, a calm evening breeze guided me back toward my home garden, landing me softly on a flower bed near the clothesline.
